# Community Challenge Brief: Last-Mile Food Waste

**Issued by:** Riverside Food Network (registered charity 1172093)
**For:** Autumn Volunteer Innovation Sprint, 7–8 November 2026

## The problem
Every week our depot receives around 14 tonnes of donated food from supermarkets. About 9% of it — mostly fresh produce and dairy — spoils before it reaches the 38 partner pantries we supply. Drivers often leave the depot with no clear picture of which pantries can take perishables that day, so chilled items sit in vans or get turned away.

## Who is affected
- Families using partner pantries, who see fewer fresh options
- Volunteer drivers, who waste time on failed drops
- Our warehouse team, who log and dispose of spoiled stock

## What we're asking for
Ideas — not necessarily software — that help match perishable stock to pantries with space and opening hours on the same day. A good solution should work for volunteers with basic phones and patchy signal.

## Constraints
- No budget for new vehicles or cold storage this year
- Pantry coordinators are volunteers; anything new must take under 5 minutes a day
- Must not require pantries to share personal data about clients

## How submissions will be judged
Impact on spoilage, ease of adoption, cost, and how quickly we could pilot it with 5 pantries.

Questions to sprint@riversidefood.example.
